title: Wide as His Vast Dominion Lies
description: Wide as His Vast Dominion Lies in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 163 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Universal Praise”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Wide as his vast do-min-ion lies, Make the Cre-a-tor's name be known; Loud as his thun-ders speak his praise, And sound it lof-ty as his throne.

lines: Wide as his vast dominion lies,
Make the Creator's name be known;
Loud as his thunders speak his praise,
And sound it lofty as his throne.
O may it dwell on every tongue;
But saints, who best have known the Lord,
Are bound to raise the noblest song.
Speak of the wonders of that love
Which Gabriel plays on every chord;
From all below, and all above,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
